canonical_statement: The highest ontological level is affirmed absolutely, without negation of a superior.

attributions.surface_quote: Negation in the upward direction ends there, for to negate this creature is not to affirm some superior creature.

canonical_statement: Existence is contingent upon being known by a higher or equal order of consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: Each is, to the extent that it is known either by itself or something higher

canonical_statement: Latent potentiality is considered non-existent until actualized in formed matter.

attributions.surface_quote: things still latent in the womb of nature... are said not to exist

canonical_statement: All instances of a created nature exist simultaneously in their ideal form, but are manifested sequentially in time and space.

attributions.surface_quote: he made them all at once in that one, first [ideal or prototype] man

canonical_statement: True existence is defined by intellectual apprehension, not by mutable material form.

attributions.surface_quote: only those things truly exist which are grasped by the intellect

canonical_statement: That which is subject to generation and corruption does not truly exist.

attributions.surface_quote: change, as is the case with all bodies subject to generation and corruption, is not said to exist in any true sense of the word.

canonical_statement: Human nature, when corrupted by sin, loses its existence and is restored to being through divine grace.

attributions.surface_quote: When it has destroyed through sin the dignity of the divine image... it is therefore said not to be. But when it is restored... then it begins to be.

canonical_statement: God is the uncreated creator of all things, the principal cause, and the ultimate end towards which all things gravitate.

attributions.surface_quote: this kind of nature is correctly predicated of God alone, for only he is understood to create all and yet is himself without any beginning or source.

canonical_statement: The divine nature is the ultimate end of all things, as they seek rest and perfection in it.

attributions.surface_quote: For all things seek him. He is then, the beginning, the middle, and the end.

canonical_statement: The divine nature is both the creator and, in a distinct sense, created.

attributions.surface_quote: they not only claim it creates all that exists, but that it is also created.

canonical_statement: The divine nature is referred to by various names, including 'God', 'Goodness', 'Essence', and 'Truth'.

attributions.surface_quote: though the divine nature is called by many names like “Goodness,” “Essence,” “Truth,” and the like, nevertheless scripture most often uses this name [viz. “God” or “theos”].

canonical_statement: The divine essence is characterized by a simultaneous, paradoxical state of absolute immobility and pervasive movement.

attributions.surface_quote: God is most truly said to be movement that is stable and stability that is mobile.

canonical_statement: The divine will is the causal principle for the existence of all things.

attributions.surface_quote: his running through all things is nothing else than seeing all things, even as it is through his seeing and flowing through all things that they come to exist through him.

canonical_statement: The divine nature is immutable and unchanging.

attributions.surface_quote: in himself, God is incapable of change; his natural immobility is never lost.

canonical_statement: The divine essence encompasses all of existence, with nothing existing outside of it.

attributions.surface_quote: he sees noth¬ing outside himself, since nothing is outside of him.

canonical_statement: The divine essence is the locus and limit of all that exists.

attributions.surface_quote: since he represents the locus and limit in which all is confined.

canonical_statement: The divine nature is the ultimate end and source of all motion and rest.

attributions.surface_quote: he is the cause of all things at rest or in motion

canonical_statement: All things naturally move towards the divine nature for eternal rest.

attributions.surface_quote: they gravitate towards him by their natural motion so that they may eventually rest in him

canonical_statement: The divine nature causes all things to transition from nonexistence to existence.

attributions.surface_quote: he makes everything 'run' from nonexistence to existence

canonical_statement: The movement of the divine nature is equivalent to the divine will to create.

attributions.surface_quote: the movement of the divine nature means nothing else than the proposal of the divine will to create

canonical_statement: In the divine nature, being and willing are identical.

attributions.surface_quote: his being and willing are one and the same

canonical_statement: The divine nature creates all things by bringing them forth from nothingness into being.

attributions.surface_quote: bringing them forth from nothing, so that they may be in being from nonbeing

canonical_statement: The divine nature is essentially the ground of all existence.

attributions.surface_quote: except for it nothing exists essentially

canonical_statement: All existence is a participation in a singular, true existence.

attributions.surface_quote: everything which is said to exist does not exist in itself, but by participating in that nature which truly exists.

canonical_statement: The divine nature is immanent in all created things, becoming knowable through them.

attributions.surface_quote: the divine nature, being invisible in itself, reveals itself in all things which exist

canonical_statement: Consciousness or intellect is actualized through engagement with sensory forms or signs.

attributions.surface_quote: when it begins to think and take form from certain sense images, it is not unreasonably said to be made.

canonical_statement: The divine essence, though transcendent, is expressed and knowable within its creations.

attributions.surface_quote: the divine essence... can justly be said to “be created” in those things which are made by it

canonical_statement: The divine essence is unknowable in its essence, yet its existence, wisdom, and life can be inferred from creation.

attributions.surface_quote: from the things it creates we know only that it subsists essentially; we do not know what its essence is

canonical_statement: Theology employs affirmative and negative methods to discuss the divine nature.

attributions.surface_quote: one affirmative... the other negative, called apofatica

canonical_statement: The negative theological method denies that the divine essence is any of the things that can be understood.

attributions.surface_quote: denies that the divine essence or substance is any of the things which exist, i.e. which can be understood

canonical_statement: The affirmative theological method predicates all existing things of the divine nature, not as being identical to them, but as their cause.

attributions.surface_quote: predicates of that nature everything which exists... suggests that all things which exist by reason of this nature can be predicated of it

canonical_statement: The ultimate nature of reality is beyond direct conceptualization and is referred to through diverse, often contradictory, metaphorical designations.

attributions.surface_quote: this ineffable nature is said to be truth, goodness, essence, light, justice, the sun, a star, wind, water, a lion, a city, a worm

canonical_statement: Attributes ascribed to the divine substance are not accidental or externally acquired but are intrinsic to its essence.

attributions.surface_quote: God has the opposite trait or that such a trait, though not part of his essence, is something he happens to have coeternally?

canonical_statement: The existence of a single, ultimate principle or source for all reality is a necessary condition for existence itself.

attributions.surface_quote: all things have not a single principle or source, but that there are two or more, each differing from the other. And this is something true reason would not hesitate to deny

canonical_statement: Divine attributes are properly predicated of God because God is not opposed by or different in nature from any other coeternal entity.

attributions.surface_quote: God to whom nothing is opposed or with whom nothing differs by nature coeternally

canonical_statement: Divine attributes predicated of God are analogical, not literal, as God transcends all oppositional categories.

attributions.surface_quote: God is said to be essence, but properly speaking he to whom nothing is opposed is not essence

canonical_statement: The divine essence is beyond all conceptualization and predication, existing as 'superessential'.

attributions.surface_quote: he is hyperousia, i.e. superessential

canonical_statement: God's nature surpasses all positive attributes, being 'more than' the concepts they represent.

attributions.surface_quote: he is hyperagathos, i.e. more than good

canonical_statement: The divine is not identical with concepts like 'truth' or 'eternity' because these concepts have negations.

attributions.surface_quote: God is not properly truth, but hyperalethes

canonical_statement: All divine names are ultimately inadequate descriptions of the divine reality.

attributions.surface_quote: The same rule must be observed in all the divine names.

canonical_statement: The ultimate nature of reality is beyond conceptualization and language.

attributions.surface_quote: no word, no name, no sensible sound could properly signify this ineffable nature

canonical_statement: Attributes like 'essence', 'truth', and 'wisdom' are applied to the divine in a transferred, not proper, sense.

attributions.surface_quote: essence, truth, wisdom... are asserted. But superessential, more than truth, more than wisdom

canonical_statement: Theology is divided into affirmative and negative approaches to understanding the divine.

attributions.surface_quote: theology is bipartite: catajatica and apojatica... affirmative and negative

canonical_statement: Affirmation and negation, though seemingly opposed, are in perfect harmony when describing the divine nature.

attributions.surface_quote: affirmation and negation... not in opposition... but in perfect harmony with each other

canonical_statement: The divine essence is beyond all proper predication and comprehension.

attributions.surface_quote: the divine essence remains bare of all proper meaning

canonical_statement: Negative theology acknowledges the divine nature is incomprehensible and ineffable.

attributions.surface_quote: the negative way which says it is not truth, clearly recognizing the divine nature to be incomprehensible and ineffable

canonical_statement: Apparent affirmations about the divine contain implicit negations.

attributions.surface_quote: although the negation does not appear in the words, it is evident to one who considers the matter carefully that it is not lacking in the understanding

canonical_statement: Statements about the divine that appear affirmative are understood through negative theology.

attributions.surface_quote: I am forced to admit the aforesaid designations which seem to lack any negation are more in harmony with negative than affirmative theology

canonical_statement: Superlative descriptions of the divine, while affirmative in form, are negative in meaning, indicating what the divine is not rather than what it is.

attributions.surface_quote: what superficially seems to lack negation is strongly negative in meaning

canonical_statement: The divine Word (Son) is the principle through which all things are created, distinct from the Father who is the principle from which all things originate.

attributions.surface_quote: The principle from which are all things is the Father, the principle through which are all things is the Son

canonical_statement: The generation of the divine Word from the Father is the foundational cause and operational execution for the creation of all things.

attributions.surface_quote: his generation from the Father is itself the establishment of the cause of all

canonical_statement: The divine Word is begotten but not made, while all other things are made but not begotten.

attributions.surface_quote: Through what was begotten but not made, all things were made but not begotten

canonical_statement: The divine substance of the Father and Son is coeternal.

attributions.surface_quote: The substance of the Father and Son is coeternal.

canonical_statement: The Son naturally precedes all created things.

attributions.surface_quote: The Son, however, does precede naturally all things which are made through him.

canonical_statement: Created things began to exist within the divine substance before worldly time, not in time but with time.

attributions.surface_quote: those things which were made through him have begun to exist in him before worldly time, not indeed in time, but with time.

canonical_statement: Time itself is a created entity, not existing prior to creation.

attributions.surface_quote: For time itself is among the other things that were made; it was not created before, but with [them].

canonical_statement: Nothing is made outside or without the divine Word.

attributions.surface_quote: without him was made nothing that has been made

canonical_statement: Only the Father and Spirit are coeternal, consubstantial, and coessential with the divine Word.

attributions.surface_quote: Nothing however is understood to be coeternal, consubstantial, or coessential with him except his Father and his Spirit

canonical_statement: The superessential divine nature is the uncreated creative cause of all that exists and does not exist.

attributions.surface_quote: this superessential nature is the creative cause of all that exists and does not exist. It itself is not created

canonical_statement: The divine nature is the single origin and fount of all things.

attributions.surface_quote: the one beginning or principle, the one universal fount and origin of all things.

canonical_statement: The divine nature is beyond being and nonbeing, transcending all categories of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: it is more than being (esse)

canonical_statement: The ultimate cause of all existence is not nothing, but rather a positive reality that transcends comprehension.

attributions.surface_quote: the cause of all things which exist be understood to be nothing

canonical_statement: Creation ex nihilo means that existence is brought forth from a state of non-existence, not from a pre-existing material or cause.

attributions.surface_quote: from the nonexistent, existent things have been made

canonical_statement: The term 'nothing' in creation ex nihilo signifies the absolute absence of any pre-existing essence or material.

attributions.surface_quote: The name then indicates the total deprivation of anything essential

canonical_statement: The negation of all essence or subsistence applies to all created things.

attributions.surface_quote: negation of all essence or subsistence of everything which in the realm of nature has been created.

canonical_statement: The Creator made all things from absolute nothingness.

attributions.surface_quote: the Creator of all creatures made those things he willed to make from absolute nothingness

canonical_statement: God and creature are not related as genus and species, or whole and part.

attributions.surface_quote: God is not a genus with respect to the creature, nor the creature a species of [what is divine or] God.

canonical_statement: Metaphorical language is used to describe the relationship between God and creation.

attributions.surface_quote: in a metaphorical sense, God is called “genus,” “whole,” “species,” and “part”

canonical_statement: The division of God and creation is an intellectual contemplation, not an actual division.

attributions.surface_quote: not as if there was an [actual] division of a genus into its forms or a whole into its parts.

canonical_statement: The first and fourth divisions of nature (referring to God) are identical.

attributions.surface_quote: the first and the fourth are one, since they both refer to God alone.

canonical_statement: God is the principle and the end of all created things.

attributions.surface_quote: he is the principle of all things that were created by him and he is also the end of all things

canonical_statement: The ultimate cause of reality creates by divine multiplication, resulting in diverse forms of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: cause of all can be said to create when those things created by him...proceed to become genera, species, and individuals

canonical_statement: All created things will ultimately return to their original cause, which is designated as the goal of all.

attributions.surface_quote: all those things which came forth from this selfsame cause will return to it as their end

canonical_statement: The ultimate cause, as the final destination of all, is beyond the processes of creation and being created.

attributions.surface_quote: it is designated as the goal of all and is referred to as neither creating nor created

canonical_statement: Upon the return of all things to the ultimate cause, existence will remain in a state of immutable rest.

attributions.surface_quote: in it all will remain at rest, and one, immutable individual

canonical_statement: The Logos or Word of the Father is the cause of all things, both visible and invisible, and the ultimate goal of the world.

attributions.surface_quote: the [Logos or] Word of the Father...is the cause of all things...is he not also the 'cause of causes' or finis of the world

canonical_statement: The desire of all creatures is ultimately directed towards the Word of God as the primary established goal.

attributions.surface_quote: everything reaching out for something has as the goal of its endeavor something which was first established in him

canonical_statement: The beginning and the end of the world are found within the Word of God.

attributions.surface_quote: the beginning and the end of the world is to be found...the beginning and end are the Word itself

canonical_statement: The Word is a multiple end without end and a beginning without a beginning, originating solely from the Father.

attributions.surface_quote: the beginning and end are the Word itself, which is a multiple end without end and a beginning without a beginning

canonical_statement: All things originate from and return to the ultimate principle, which is both the beginning and the end.

attributions.surface_quote: The one from whom and unto whom are all things, for he is both beginning and end

canonical_statement: The entirety of creation originates from, proceeds through, and returns to God.

attributions.surface_quote: from him and through him and unto him are all things

canonical_statement: The origin, return, and reunion of all creation are structured through divisions that ultimately resolve into God.

attributions.surface_quote: the origin of all that was made...also the return and reunion...resolution of the whole of creation into one and ultimately into God himself

canonical_statement: Nature is divided into the created and the uncreated (God).

attributions.surface_quote: the first of all the divisions of nature is that which separates the created from what is not created, i.e. God.

canonical_statement: The created realm is divided into the sensible and the intelligible.

attributions.surface_quote: The second divides the created into the sensible and the intelligible.

canonical_statement: The sensible world is divided into heaven and earth.

attributions.surface_quote: The third differentiates the sensible world into heaven and earth.

canonical_statement: Man, composed of body and soul, unifies the spiritual and corporeal realms.

attributions.surface_quote: he is also referred to as a mediator, for composed as he is of body and soul, he holds in himself widely divergent extremes, namely the spiritual and the corporeal, and gives them unity.

canonical_statement: All posterior creation is contained within man.

attributions.surface_quote: for all that was posterior to God is contained in man.

canonical_statement: The dissolution of the body returns it to the elements from which it originated.

attributions.surface_quote: when the body is dissolved and summoned [in death] to return to the four elements of the sensible world from which it was called.

canonical_statement: The body is reconstituted from the common fund of elements during resurrection.

attributions.surface_quote: when each one receives back his own body from the common fund of the four elements.

canonical_statement: The body is transformed into spirit.

attributions.surface_quote: when the body is transformed into spirit.

canonical_statement: Visible matter originates from invisible elemental factors.

attributions.surface_quote: matter is nothing else than a kind of combination of what is accidental, such that visible matter comes from elemental factors that are themselves invisible.

canonical_statement: The dissolubility of matter implies it contains nothing immutable.

attributions.surface_quote: Therefore there is nothing in it which cannot be dissolved.

canonical_statement: Bodies can be created from and dissolved into incorporeal causes.

attributions.surface_quote: bodies can be created from incorporeal causes and can be dissolved into them again.

canonical_statement: The ultimate destiny of all existence is a hierarchical transmutation and reunion, culminating in unity with the Creator.

attributions.surface_quote: the destiny or goal of all things visible and invisible

canonical_statement: Transmutation involves the elevation of the inferior into the superior, not annihilation.

attributions.surface_quote: it is always the inferior that is transmuted into the superior

canonical_statement: The return to the Creator preserves the essence of created substances.

attributions.surface_quote: not by a confusion or annihilation of their essences or substances

canonical_statement: Understanding leads to unity with the object of understanding.

attributions.surface_quote: everything which understands in a pure fashion becomes one with that which it understands

canonical_statement: The union of nature with God is an elevation, not a destruction of substance.

attributions.surface_quote: change of human nature into God should not be thought of as a destruction

canonical_statement: Archetypal ideas possess an intentional mode of existence characteristic of pure thought objects, existing timelessly but not strictly eternally.

attributions.surface_quote: ideas can only be called “coeternal” in a secondary or derivative sense

canonical_statement: The substance of a body is fundamentally intelligible, allowing for the reunification of intelligible substances.
Human beings share a common genus or stock with the divine.

attributions.surface_quote: as children of God, men are of the same race or stock (genus) as God

canonical_statement: Human nature was created with a material body and a visible universe to facilitate transcendence and a return to a primordial state.

attributions.surface_quote: God created man with a material body in a visible universe so that by transcending its limitation he might return to the state originally planned by God

canonical_statement: An idealized, sexless form of human nature did not historically exist.

attributions.surface_quote: this idealized and sexless form of human nature never actually existed

canonical_statement: Philosophy is a tool of the devil, unless subservient to theology.

attributions.surface_quote: Pure philosophy was an invention of the devil.

canonical_statement: Theological truth is superior to philosophical inquiry.

attributions.surface_quote: philosophy must always be kept in its place as a handmaid or servant.

canonical_statement: The unchangeability of the past is a logical consequence of speech, not a feature of reality.

attributions.surface_quote: why the past is said to be unchangeable

canonical_statement: Necessity and impossibility in discussions of the past refer to linguistic logic, not inherent properties of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: necessity and impossibility in this context do not refer to the nature of things

canonical_statement: Statements about reality, regardless of tense, express possibilities that are logically consistent.

attributions.surface_quote: it is always something possible

canonical_statement: The nature of divine reality necessitates an ideal language capable of expressing its attributes without limitation.

attributions.surface_quote: ideal language adequate to the timeless reality that is God

canonical_statement: Divine existence is characterized by a timeless mode of being.

attributions.surface_quote: God's timeless mode of existence

canonical_statement: Divine omnipotence implies the absence of any limitations on divine capability.

attributions.surface_quote: impossible even to state that there is something God cannot do

canonical_statement: Divine omnipotence is limited by divine will.

attributions.surface_quote: God can do none of the things that he does not wish to do

canonical_statement: The divine will is the ultimate determinant of divine action.

attributions.surface_quote: God does not wish it. To which I replied: If God can do none of the things that he does not wish to do

canonical_statement: The divine capacity to act is equivalent to the divine will to act.

attributions.surface_quote: God can do none of the things that he does not wish to do, he does nothing but that which he wishes

canonical_statement: Divine will is the ultimate cause of all existence, with all created things existing essentially within the divine will prior to manifestation.

attributions.surface_quote: all created things, before appearing in their visible forms, were already truly and essentially alive in the will of their Creator.

canonical_statement: Divine inability to perform certain actions stems not from a lack of power, but from the perfection of divine will and nature.

attributions.surface_quote: God does not perform because he is unwilling, and because he does not so wish, he is unable.

canonical_statement: Statements describing divine limitations in scripture are allegorical, not literal, and must be interpreted with caution to avoid theological error.

attributions.surface_quote: statements having mystical and allegorical significance, we should accept them cautiously

canonical_statement: Divine ignorance of evil is not a lack of knowledge, but a consequence of divine goodness and unwillingness to engage in evil.

attributions.surface_quote: he cannot do anything that is evil, he does not know how to do evil.

canonical_statement: All existence originates from the divine will and design.

attributions.surface_quote: by your will they have their being and were created

canonical_statement: The divine will is the efficient cause of restoration and return to integrity.

attributions.surface_quote: will is the cause whereby those things that have been lost might return

canonical_statement: Divine omnipotence implies the capacity for restoration of lost states, including moral purity.

attributions.surface_quote: God from restoring a virgin after she has fallen

canonical_statement: Divine forgiveness can overcome past transgressions, restoring purity.

attributions.surface_quote: return to me, says the Lord... I will no longer remember any of your sins

canonical_statement: The divine power can restore a state of being that has been lost, as if it had never ceased to exist.

attributions.surface_quote: God has power to restore virginity... as she was when taken from her mother's womb.

canonical_statement: Divine omnipotence extends to causing that which was made to become as if it never existed, without negating its past existence.

attributions.surface_quote: can he act so that things that were made become things that were not made?

canonical_statement: Divine action creates being from non-being, and does not annihilate being.

attributions.surface_quote: what God makes is something; what God does not make is nothing.

canonical_statement: The existence of evil or corrupt beings is a form of non-being or belonging to nothingness.

attributions.surface_quote: they belonged rather to nonbeing than to real being.

canonical_statement: Evil is a negation of existence, lacking the grounds for being provided by the Creator.

attributions.surface_quote: if whatever happened was evil, it was not something but nothing.

canonical_statement: God's creative act is the sole source of existence for all things.

attributions.surface_quote: not one thing had its being but through him.

canonical_statement: God's omnipotence and omniscience are coeternal attributes, encompassing all time.

attributions.surface_quote: ability to do all things is coeternal to God... and his power to know all things

canonical_statement: God's wisdom eternally contains and confirms all past, present, and future events.

attributions.surface_quote: contains, determines, and forever confirms within the compass of his wisdom all times

canonical_statement: The divine nature embodies an eternal, unchanging present.

attributions.surface_quote: in him there exists that eternal today that never ends; in him an everlasting present

canonical_statement: God's power is immutable and coeternal with God, existing as perpetual potency.

attributions.surface_quote: God's potency which is coeternal to him remains forever fixed and immutable.

canonical_statement: God's present is not subject to temporal succession or change.

attributions.surface_quote: his present never turns into the past, his today does not change into tomorrow

canonical_statement: For God, all possibilities are eternally present and accessible.

attributions.surface_quote: whatever God could do, he also can do, because his present never turns into the past

canonical_statement: Divine being is characterized by everlasting presence rather than past or future states.

attributions.surface_quote: as there is with him no being and having been, but only everlasting being

canonical_statement: Divine potency is characterized by perpetual, unchanging ability rather than past or future states.

attributions.surface_quote: there is no having been able and being able, but always a perpetual potency that can never change

canonical_statement: Divine potency is immutable and eternal, co-existent with the divine essence.

attributions.surface_quote: God's potency cannot be changed, it eternally endures firm and immutable.

canonical_statement: The divine being is unchanging across all temporal distinctions.

attributions.surface_quote: God is always the same and is always what he is.

canonical_statement: Divine omnipotence extends to the possibility of non-existence for all created things.

attributions.surface_quote: God could have caused things not to exist before anything was made.

canonical_statement: The temporal passage of events does not alter the eternal divine capacity to act.

attributions.surface_quote: The diversity of times does not suggest the presence of the slightest change in eternity.

canonical_statement: Divine omnipotence is absolute and without exception, encompassing all possibilities.

attributions.surface_quote: God is able to do all things, either in respect to events that have happened or not happened.

canonical_statement: The necessity of existence applies to past, present, and future events.

attributions.surface_quote: everything that happened necessarily had to happen

canonical_statement: The logical structure of reality dictates that what is, must exist, and what will be, must occur.

attributions.surface_quote: for whatever is, it is impossible not to be

canonical_statement: The concept of 'indifferent alternatives' is more accurately understood in relation to the variable nature of phenomena than to logical necessity.

attributions.surface_quote: indifferent alternatives more properly in relation to the variable nature of things

canonical_statement: The existence of God can be demonstrated through a single, self-evident argument.

attributions.surface_quote: find a single argument... which would suffice by itself

canonical_statement: The divine being is the highest good and necessary for all existence.

attributions.surface_quote: he is the highest good... needed for the existence and well-being of all else

canonical_statement: Certain truths about the divine nature are knowable through faith and reason.

attributions.surface_quote: reasoning with himself... understand what he believes

canonical_statement: Belief is a prerequisite for understanding spiritual truths.

attributions.surface_quote: Unless I believe, I shall not understand!

canonical_statement: The divine nature is beyond the full comprehension of the human mind.

attributions.surface_quote: my mind is no match for it

canonical_statement: Existence in the understanding is distinct from existence in reality.

attributions.surface_quote: it is one thing for something to be in the understanding and quite another to understand that the thing in question exists.

canonical_statement: The concept of a maximally great being can exist in the understanding.

attributions.surface_quote: in his understanding at least there is something than which nothing greater can be conceived

attributions.surface_quote: whatever is understood is in the understanding.

attributions.surface_quote: a being greater than which nothing can be conceived exists both in the understanding and in reality

canonical_statement: Existence in reality is greater than existence solely in the understanding.

attributions.surface_quote: one could also think of it as existing in reality and this is something greater

attributions.surface_quote: if it were there only, one could also think of it as existing in reality and this is something greater

attributions.surface_quote: it cannot be thought of as not existing

canonical_statement: The nature of the supreme being is such that it cannot be surpassed in conception.

attributions.surface_quote: the thing than which none greater can be thought

attributions.surface_quote: you alone have existence in the truest and highest sense

attributions.surface_quote: so evident to a reasoning mind that of all things you exist

canonical_statement: The concept of a maximally great being implies its necessary existence in reality.

attributions.surface_quote: a thing is greater if it also exists in reality than if it were in the understanding alone

attributions.surface_quote: I am not said to think of what I hear or have it in thought, but to understand it

attributions.surface_quote: the only way I can think of this being is to understand it, i.e. to include in my knowledge of it the fact that it exists

attributions.surface_quote: it would do away, for one thing, with the distinction between what is temporally prior
